defaultSuiteSkips: Eight opt-in volume/chaos/soak/replay/shutdown cases were exercised separately; six pre-existing disabled cases remain unexecuted.

extendedScenarios.resolution: Test ledger sampled closure too late after fail-fast startup. Counts now surround the actual close boundary; a negative control still rejects unauthorized stops. Production code unchanged.

soak.limits: Ten-minute synthetic lifecycle/capture fault workload, not overnight soak, real exchange traffic, sustained replay chaos, or a leak/latency proof. Successful long-run raw traces were not persisted; the separately exported 30-second run is bundled.

volume.limits: Publisher credit-pacing is test-driven; overload intentionally exercises the existing 10ms spin-and-drop policy. These are correctness checks, not peak throughput benchmarks.

Published stress work through 8d1b1ee was reviewed. The additional ControlPlaneSoakStressTest drift probe was deferred: insufficient samples can pass and inherited audit-capacity settings confound heap growth. Its original source remains on stress/control-plane.
runtimeChangesAfterSoak: Two replay-only fixes followed the ten-minute soak: version identity publication ordering/bounded waiting, and linear in-memory replay-store append. They were qualified with deterministic regressions, the final full suite, 30-second scoped replay and the final benchmark. The ten-minute soak was not repeated on the final commit.

replayAndShutdown.limits: Successful replay covers the three boot anchors, not dynamic processor incarnations or historical service churn. Unavailable service incarnations remain fail-closed. Shutdown deadlines often expire in feed stopping; not every configured blocked callback is reached on the first attempt. Direct callback-blocking regressions cover those paths separately.

replayStoreAllocation.scope: current-thread append allocation in InMemoryReplayStore; not end-to-end per-event allocation or a zero-GC claim

initialBenchmark.normalization: Both builds use Fluxtion runtime 1.1.2 and the same corrected padded-counter benchmark; throughputOnly; five independent JVM forks per build in alternating AB/BA order, 2 warm-up and 7 measured rounds of 2M events per fork; BusySpin feed/processor agents. No qualification stress test ran concurrently.
initialBenchmark.conclusion: No consistent 12% regression reproduced here. High variation and unpinned heterogeneous-core macOS prevent resolving the earlier finding; Linux pinned-core confirmation remains open. No allocation or GC claim from this throughput benchmark.
